title: Low-privileged /test/user/save stores attacker-controlled UserEntity entries in a process-lifetime static LinkedHashMap
source: authenticated low-privilege HTTP request parameters userId, username, password, mobile
sink: TestController.users.put(user.getUserId(), user) where users is private static final LinkedHashMap
driver: distinct userId values and UserEntity field sizes
retention: process-lifetime static map; entries survive across requests until process restart or explicit delete
bound: no capacity limit, TTL, eviction, per-client quota, rate limit, or @PreAuthorize permission guard; only requires authentication
impact: low-privileged default authenticated users can drive unbounded process heap growth; dynamic OOM/GC/service-unavailable threshold not measured
static_poc: Login as a default low-privilege user, then repeatedly POST /test/user/save with increasing userId and large username/password/mobile values.
dynamic_probe: Measure JVM heap, GC, /test/user/list latency, map growth, HTTP failures, and process exit under repeated saves.
